subject: Post-call: Clearlines cost synthesis, levers & proposed pilot path
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Asha Narayan <asha@clearlines.com>; Tom Reed <tom.reed@clearlines.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Clearlines cost synthesis, levers & proposed pilot path

Hi Asha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick synthesis from our call and where we recommend starting so we can move from discovery to an actionable pilot: 

Key pains you confirmed
- Unpredictable per-transaction inference spend across peak hours and new product funnels (esp. refunds flow).
- Latency spikes when traffic bursts cause fallbacks to larger models; that degrades UX.
- Lack of instrumentation in the current stack to separate model costs vs infra (hard to forecast monthly spend).

Goals you called out
- Hold cost-per-transaction below $0.004 on average while serving ~120 req/s during peak shopping hours.
- Keep 95th percentile latency <= 180ms for the primary inference route.
- Run a 6-week pilot focused on a single funnel (refund triage) and measure unit economics and error rate change.

Primary cost levers we discussed
1) Batching + request-awareness: 2–3x token efficiency during peak windows for short-context transactions.
2) Prefix/KV caching for repetitive prompts (refund categories) to reduce decoder cost per request by ~30–50% on hotspot traffic.
3) Model family selection + quantization for lower unit cost while validating quality on your prompt set.
4) Routing by policy: cheaper model for low-SLA routes, higher-tier for interactive flows.

Immediate suggested next steps (proposed timeline)
- I'll send a short TCO worksheet (attached) we can fill with your recent telemetry (avg tokens, peak qps, error budget). Target: you and Tom provide last 30 days of traffic by Friday.
- Redwood will draft a 6-week pilot scope + expected savings scenarios (baseline vs batching + cache vs dedicated capacity) — draft to you by Wednesday.
- Quick follow-up call next Tuesday to align pilot success metrics and procurement path (we’ll include procurement in that meeting).

Attachments: Clearlines_TCO_worksheet.xlsx (worksheet to populate baseline numbers)

If that matches your readout, reply with the telemetry export or a time for next week’s sync and we’ll lock in resources.

Thanks —

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

From: Asha Narayan <asha@clearlines.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@clearlines.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Clearlines cost synthesis, levers & proposed pilot path

Thanks Hannah — this is a very clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can share anonymized traffic and token stats for the refunds funnel; I’ll have that exported by EOD Thursday.
- Budget constraints: our Q4 pilots are capped at $40k total for third-party inference spend unless we can show >2x ROI within 8 weeks.
- Latency target: 95th <= 180ms is acceptable but ideally we’d like to be <=150ms for mobile flows.

Procurement: looping in Tom. He handles procurement for pilot approvals (tom.reed@clearlines.com). He’ll need a high-level SOW and an estimate by next Wednesday to fast-track.

Asha
Head of Product
Clearlines Payments
asha@clearlines.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Asha Narayan <asha@clearlines.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@clearlines.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Clearlines cost synthesis, levers & proposed pilot path

Appreciate the quick turn, Asha. Noted on the $40k cap and the tighter mobile latency preference — we’ll model scenarios for both 150ms and 180ms 95th p95 targets.

Next actions from Redwood (we’ll deliver by Wed EOD PT):
- Pilot SOW (6 weeks) with milestone gating and a success metric: net unit cost reduction >= 25% vs baseline while maintaining false-positive rate change < 1.5% absolute for refund classification.
- Three TCO scenarios in the worksheet: (A) baseline on your current model + infra; (B) batching + prefix cache on hosted Redwood; (C) dedicated capacity + quantized model. We’ll include estimated monthly run-rate and expected delta for 6-week pilot.
- Quick checklist for procurement: template SOW, insurance/KMS notes, SOC2 evidence link.

Attached: pilot_scope_and_metrics.pdf (SOW draft) and the TCO worksheet filled with Redwood assumptions — please replace the traffic numbers when you have the export.

If this looks right I’ll schedule a 30-minute decision sync for next Tuesday 10:00am PT and include procurement. Want to confirm that time now?

Best —
Hannah

[Attachment: pilot_scope_and_metrics.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: Clearlines_TCO_worksheet.xlsx (excel)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Clearlines pilot prep — pre-work and asks

Ben / Marissa — quick internal note after Asha’s reply and the draft SOW: 

Priority pre-work
- Ben: can you run the cost model using our medium-latency quantized profile (Q4-quant-v2) and the caching assumptions (30% decoder savings on refund funnel) and paste the three-scenario numbers into the worksheet by EOD Monday? Use baseline tokens = 22 avg, peak qps = 120, 95th latency goal = 150ms and 180ms variants.
- Marissa: I’ll own scheduling the decision sync with Clearlines (propose Tue 10am PT) and prepare a 1-slide procurement brief (SOW highlights + insurance/SOC links) for Tom.

Key constraints to keep in mind: Clearlines will not exceed $40k for the pilot without an explicit exec approval. We need to present a plausible path to >2x ROI within 8 weeks or a fallback option where we demonstrate enough operational gains to justify extended spend.

I’ve attached the SOW and worksheet we sent them for your reference (drive link in metadata). I’ll include updated numbers once Ben posts the scenario outputs.

Thanks —
Hannah
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
